slides.slide_title: Introduce silent letter pairs: kn wr gn
slides.teacher_cue: Three letter pairs where the first letter is silent. kn = /n/: know, knock, knee, knife. wr = /r/: write, wrap, wrong, wrist. gn = /n/: gnat, gnaw, sign (silent gn at end). Historical note: these letters were once pronounced — kn was k+n, wr was w+r. The pronunciation simplified but the spelling stayed. Students must memorise: k is silent before n, w is silent before r, g is silent before n.
slides.expected_response: Students read kn, wr, and gn words correctly by applying the silent letter rules.
slides.correction_move: Establish each rule: kn — say the n, the k is silent. wr — say the r, the w is silent. gn — say the n, the g is silent. Students sort words into three groups.
slides.observation_note: Watch for students pronouncing the silent letter — producing /kn/, /wr/, or /gn/.

slides.observation_note: Listen for whether students can carry the focus from isolation into a real word.

slides.teacher_cue: Say know — to be aware of. k is silent — kn = /n/. Reveal and blend.

slides.correction_move: Model know orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for silent k — only /n/ is produced.

slides.correction_move: Model knee orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for silent k and long /iː/ in ee.

slides.observation_note: Watch for silent w and /r/ at start.

slides.teacher_cue: Say wrong — not right. w is silent, wr = /r/, ng coda. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say wrong orally and connect meaning before blending.
slides.correction_move: Model wrong orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for silent w and /ŋ/ at end.
